content.comment_body: Hello! I have a [product_name] and two [product_name] modules dedicated to PT100 sensors. Initially, I grounded the shields of the cables by connecting them to PE, but I noticed the input values were unstable. After disconnecting the shields from PE, the readings became steady. Is this expected behavior?
Did you follow the approach shown in this reference? [url]

Yes, I followed the instructions as illustrated, connecting both the PE conductor and cable shielding to the PE terminal on the module. However, I'm unsure of what is meant by 'ungrounded power supply.' Should I link the M terminal of the power supply to the PE conductor? The fluctuations were minor (roughly ±0.25°C), but they were bothersome since message texts kept showing varying readings.

Hello, here are some quick points: - How long are your measuring wires? It's best they don't exceed 10 meters (or 30 feet). - Is your equipment or cabinet properly grounded? Without a good ground, the shield may act as an antenna, picking up noise; inspect the wall socket to be certain. - If no ground is available, connect the M wire of your 24VDC supply to the module's ground. - Also, be aware that the minimum resolution is 0.25°C, and since there's no hardware filter (only possible through software methods as discussed elsewhere), you shouldn't expect much more improvement. Good luck!

Thanks for your response. The measurement wires are about 7 meters long. I can't confirm whether the ground quality is good, as that part of the installation wasn't my responsibility. I use a common ground for both the main electrical setup and the modules, which I believe is the correct method.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report minor but noticeable fluctuations (±0.25°C) in input readings from PT100 sensors connected to [product_name] modules, specifically when cable shields are grounded to PE. Detaching the shield from PE leads to more stable readings, prompting queries regarding correct grounding practices and expectations of signal stability. The hardware’s measurement resolution limits and lack of built-in filtering contribute to the underlying issue, creating some annoyance with displayed fluctuating values.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate stable, non-fluctuating input readings, particularly when following documented wiring standards for grounding cable shields.
